## 1. The question, frozen

The title and the opening scene make one question central: **is Time a fourth dimension of Space, and can a machine carry a person along it?** The chapters are explicit that this is the one, and the narration (chapters IV–VI) is a second question — what the far future is like — that he has not yet explained.

- **Range:** claimed everywhere, for "any real body", shown once in a Richmond drawing-room.
- **Asked:** does the conclusion follow (an argument), and what can we tell from the vanishing?

## 4. Whole-explanation checks

- **Flip.** Had the model stayed on the table, the geometry would stand untouched: no moving part ties it to the demonstration. Had it gone to the past, the same words cover it. The demonstration explains almost nothing; the argument answers to its own premise.
- **Direction.** Backwards. He begins at "it vanished" and reads off "into time". Poke the lever and only the report moves; poke the outcome and nothing moves in the lever.
- **J3 is the loose bolt.** The candle going out is a change to the world his account has no part for. The Medical Man "laid considerable stress" on it and it was never taken up.
- **Pull.** *Fixed and unalterable* versus *the driver determines direction* — one must give; he drops the first in silence. *Diluted presentation* versus *the dusty coat and cut chin*: the first requires that time-travelling be imperceptible, the second requires it to leave gross marks on cloth and skin. Those two lines are drawn straight through each other.
- **Catch-alls and gauges.** Three bins, no gauge on any: "diluted presentation", "into the Unknown", "I don't know which".
- **The change list leaves out** where the model now is, how he got back, why the candle went out, and whether he aged. It also leaves out a case his own house supplies: the ghost trick of last Christmas, which everyone saw and which was a trick.
- **Rival: conjuring.** Nothing on the list separates it from the machine except his word and his dusty coat — and the rival supplies both. At this level they are one explanation until the model is shown a second time.
- **Where the parts came from.** The barometer argument is the one *built* piece. The psychology and the threshold are *borrowed*. "Fixed and unalterable" is *asserted*. The machine is the owner's *assertion*. "No trickery" is *fixed*. "I don't know which" is *fitted* to whichever way it went.

## 5. What would make it harder to vary

Two moves, and they are the same move twice: **put a number on the threshold** — state the speed and exactly what a bystander would see; a reading that would worry him is the gauge his catch-all lacks — and **exhibit the model a second time**, so the conjuring rival and the machine rival part company.

## 6. What this does not show

Passing is not truth, and failing is not falsehood. This is fiction, so the machine's world is stipulated; what the tests find is where his case is held by argument and where by assertion. And I have read only six chapters: the Eloi and the Morlocks — the book's real explanation of a society — have not been given yet.

## 7. One next step

Ask the Time Traveller for the reading: at fifty times our rate, what does a man standing at the table actually see, and at what number would he conclude the machine did *not* go?
